subject: environmental-science
title: Pollution & Acid Rain: How Acid Rain Forms
welcome_lead: When pollution meets clouds, rain can fall sour.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: acid rain causes, effects, solutions.
final_note: Less burning, less acid rain — it really is that simple.

concepts.def: Rain made acidic by gas pollution.
Soft rock that acid rain eats away.
Device that cleans gases before they escape.

walkthroughs.body_html: Burning fuels releases sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. These dissolve in cloud water to make acid. The rain that falls is more acidic than normal.
Acid rain damages forests, kills fish in lakes by lowering pH, and eats away at limestone buildings and statues.
Burn cleaner fuels. Add scrubbers to power-station chimneys. Use catalytic converters in cars. Acid rain in the UK has fallen a lot since the 1990s.

mcqs.q: Acid rain is made worse by burning:
Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.
It creates new carbon that did not exist before.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
